svg.aria-label: The User Experience System: six layers from base tokens up to screens, each built only from the layer beneath, with what each holds, who owns it, and which check judges it and when; the stylesheet and components publish to design.md and Claude Design; a bottom band shows what runs at every edit, at commit, at the end of a body of work, at deploy, on request and at a kit release.
svg.font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: The User Experience System — layers, owners, checks
Each layer is made only from the layers beneath it. The kit owns the kinds, the words and the checks. The project owns every value, block, recipe and rule. The human approves what is new.
LAYER · WHAT IT HOLDS
OWNER
CHECKED BY · WHEN
Screens
routes/ and features/: a route follows one recipe and fills its slots with content:
wording, data, server calls. Draws no box, writes no raw value, owns no behaviour.
// ui-recipe: <recipe>.md // ui-content
project
token check · commit, CI, changed lines — no box, no raw value, no faded colour, no frame atom
judge · commit, advisory — FOLLOWS-RULE, REPAINT, SCREEN-BOX, TOKEN-AGAINST-PURPOSE
status check · commit, deploy — the header names a recipe that exists
human · end of work — an exception on one screen is theirs: design-accepted — reason
Recipes and behaviour rules
A recipe: how one page type is put together — its frame (a block) plus instructions,
each a closed pick. A behaviour rule: how the app acts on one topic, everywhere.
kind: recipe · frame · reference kind: behaviour · code: [...] block-types: apps:
project
status check · commit, deploy — a kind, a frame that exists, a reference screen, apps that exist
token check · commit, CI — every role, token and component a rule names exists
judge · commit, advisory — RULE-REACH, RULE-CONFLICT, TOKEN-AGAINST-PURPOSE
human · end of work — a new recipe or rule is pending until approved
Blocks
components/: one block per block type, built from atoms and blocks. Owns its look,
inner layout and guarantees; carries variants, props and slots. A page type's block is a frame.
// ui-block: <Type> // ui-behaviour: <rule>.md (the type list is the kit's)
project
types: kit
status check · commit, deploy — type on the list, header and inventory agree, one block per type
judge · commit, advisory — DUPLICATE-BLOCK, NAMED-FOR-DATA, VARIANT-INCOMPLETE
compare-ui-values · end of work — proves a change left every visible value the same
human · end of work — a new block or variant is pending until approved
Atoms
components/ui/: one control or element that owns its look — a button, an input, a badge.
Vendored from shadcn and restyled once, at the source, onto the project's roles.
// ui-atom
project
token check · commit, CI — every class a role, restyled once; arbitrary spacing never
status check · commit, deploy — listed in the inventory's atoms table
a11y rules · every edit, CI — type on buttons, names on icon buttons, focus visible
Role tokens
The stylesheets: a name for each job — row-title, control, feedback-danger — each with a
purpose comment. Only roles are used outside the token files. Named for the job, not the size.
--color-* --radius-* --spacing-* --shadow-* @utility type-*
project
token check · commit, CI — resolves, is reached, light and dark agree, 4.5:1 contrast,
commented, never named by size, generated files current
judge · commit, advisory — ROLE-NAME, DUPLICATE-ROLE
human · end of work — a new role is pending until approved
Base tokens
The theme's palette and scale, usually a tweakcn export: a light block and a dark block.
The one place a look is chosen by eye. Not published: wrapped in publish: off … publish: on.
:root { … } .dark { … }
project
or a Design Pack
token check · commit, CI — every value resolves to a plain colour or length
build step · app build — plain-colour fallbacks added for browsers without oklch
made only from
PUBLISHED FROM THE STYLESHEET AND THE COMPONENTS · NEVER EDITED THERE
design.md
token section generated between the publish
markers; the prose is hand-written
Claude Design system
tokens, atoms and blocks bundled; a design
built on it comes back to the code as changes
token check · commit, CI — design.md and the generated files are current
render check · publish — every component renders in light, dark and canvas mounting
WHEN
every UI edit
the skill reads the inventory,
the recipe and the rules, and
builds from the system; a gap
is built pending, never
asked about mid-build
/commit · /ship-main
token check and status check
gate; the judge answers one
yes/no per candidate, three
times; a yes is a pending item;
no commit is refused on taste
end of a body of work
compare-ui-values proves what
did not change; the human sees
each pending item as the real
thing: approve · defer · fix;
rivals go on a comparison page
/deploy
refuses while anything is
pending; deferred blocks
nothing, and is pending
again once its code changes
on request
/design-audit asks the same
questions over a whole layer,
bottom up; each yes is settled
with the human, one at a time
kit release
every judge question runs its
invented cases, three times
each; one that drifts from the
known answer is rewritten
or dropped

Status words, the same everywhere: pending waits for the human and blocks deploy · approved is the human's word alone · deferred is "not looked at, trusted": blocks nothing, pending again when the code changes.
